items.prompt: A full bounded heap retains the 3 largest values so far, with root 5. A new value 8 arrives. What follows from the retention invariant?

options.text: Always discard 8 because the heap is full
options.why: That would lose one of the largest observed values.
The contract retains three observations, not three copies of the newest.

options.text: Replace the root with 8 and restore the heap
options.why: The prior smallest retained value is the one to discard.

options.text: Sort only the new value without comparing the root
options.why: The boundary comparison decides whether retention should change.

items.explanation: A min-heap of the largest k values exposes the current cutoff at its root. A larger incoming value displaces that cutoff.
